description:
lib/string.fz: duplicate(s, n) is s <> duplicate(s, n - 1), so the result is rebuilt n times and n copies of a k-byte string copy k*n*n/2 bytes; it is also body-recursive n deep. String.duplicate("abcdefghij", 2_000_000) on PR #585's build was killed after about 16 s of CPU. Elixir's String.duplicate is :binary.copy, one copy.
Change: build by doubling (duplicate(s, n) = half <> half, plus s when n is odd), so the bytes copied are about twice the result and the depth is log n; or a runtime copy primitive if doubling measures poorly.
Signal: an oracle fixture duplicates to several megabytes on interp, run and build and checks size and content against Elixir; allocation bytes pinned near twice the result.
title: String.duplicate copies each byte a bounded number of times
